problems.section_subtitle: Farmers face silent, invisible field challenges every day. Traditional scouting is slow and manual.
problems.p1_desc: Farmers usually spot pests only after leaves, stems, or fruits show visible damage—often too late for gentle intervention.
problems.p2_desc: Lack of early warnings leads to calendar-based spraying or excessive chemical use, increasing costs and pest resistance.
problems.p3_desc: Without precise microclimate data, fields suffer either water stress or wasteful over-watering from unguided irrigation.
problems.p4_desc: Physical field scouting requires heavy labour and cannot provide 24/7 observation when insects are most active at night or dawn.

solution.title: How AgriVigil Works: 4 Continuous Steps
solution.subtitle: Sense -> Analyse -> Predict -> Act: empowering preventive crop stewardship.
solution.step1_desc: Field-deployed units continuously listen for microscopic insect vibrations, while monitoring temperature and relative humidity.
solution.step2_desc: Raw acoustic frequencies and microclimate readings are filtered to separate environmental sounds from biological activity.
solution.step3_desc: Intelligent algorithms assess pest infestation risk and evaluate crop water requirements based on real microclimate trends.
solution.step4_desc: Clear, actionable advisories reach the farmer's phone via SMS, WhatsApp, or voice, enabling timely preventive action.

how_page.title: How the AgriVigil Technology Works
how_page.subtitle: An honest, inside look into our acoustic sensing, microclimate integration, and alert pipeline.
how_page.acoustic_title: Acoustic Sensing: Listening to the Soil and Canopy
how_page.acoustic_desc: Insects generate minute vibrational and acoustic signals when feeding, chewing, flying, or boring into stems. AgriVigil employs high-sensitivity acoustic transducers tuned to specific biological frequency windows.
how_page.acoustic_disclaimer: *Note: Species-level acoustic classification is a development target currently being trained and verified in controlled trials.
how_page.irrigation_desc: By continuously recording ambient temperature and relative humidity, the system calculates vapor pressure deficit (VPD) and crop heat stress trends. This helps growers prevent water wastage and avoid drought stress.
how_page.sample_alert_body: AgriVigil Alert for Field #2 (Cotton): Possible pest activity detected in south corner. Inspect leaves and boll stems before spraying. Temperature: 32°C, Humidity: 68%.
how_page.challenges_title: The Real-World Engineering Challenges We're Solving
how_page.challenges_subtitle: Agriculture is noisy and unpredictable. Here is our honest R&D stance on what we are tackling in the field:
how_page.researcher_note: Technical specifications: Acoustic bandwidth 50 Hz - 20 kHz with hardware bandpass filtering. Microclimate sampling at 15-minute intervals. Edge inferencing on low-power microcontrollers with sub-GHz or cellular telemetry.

challenges.c1_desc: Wind gusts and rain droplets create high-amplitude acoustic background noise. We are developing specialized acoustic baffles and DSP spectral subtraction filters.
challenges.c2_title: Bird, Animal, and Farm Machinery Noise
challenges.c2_desc: Tractors, diesel pumps, and birds introduce low and mid-frequency interference. Our algorithms isolate persistent, characteristic feeding signals from transient machinery spikes.
challenges.c3_desc: Real fields host beneficial insects alongside harmful pests. We are building comparative acoustic datasets to learn distinctive bio-acoustic signatures.
challenges.c4_desc: Sound travels differently through leafy cabbage than through rigid sugarcane or woody orchard branches. We are testing acoustic attenuation across various crop architectures.
challenges.c5_title: Temperature & Humidity Impact on Insect Activity
challenges.c5_desc: Insects are ectothermic; their feeding and movement rates fluctuate with ambient temperature. We correlate acoustic thresholds directly with simultaneous microclimate data.
challenges.c6_title: Lab Signal vs. Harsh Field Conditions
challenges.c6_desc: A quiet laboratory soundproof box differs vastly from a dusty, humid monsoon farm. That is why our focus is rigorous real-field validation during pilots.

roadmap_page.title: Where We Are Today: 9-Stage R&D Roadmap
roadmap_page.subtitle: We believe in total transparency. Follow our structured progression from acoustic prototype to commercial deployment.
roadmap_page.metrics_title: What We Will Measure During Field Pilots
roadmap_page.metrics_subtitle: We do not claim results before testing. These are the explicit quantitative metrics our pilot deployments will track:

roadmap_stages.stage1_desc: Designing the transducer hardware, acoustic enclosure, and high-gain low-noise amplification circuitry.
roadmap_stages.stage2_desc: Recording insect feeding, movement, and flight patterns under calibrated lab and enclosure conditions.
roadmap_stages.stage3_desc: Investigating whether target pest species exhibit distinct, classifiable frequency characteristics.
roadmap_stages.stage4_desc: Integrating precision microclimate sensors into the field-deployable weather-resistant unit.
roadmap_stages.stage5_desc: Deploying units into active agricultural plots to validate acoustic propagation and mechanical durability.
roadmap_stages.stage6_desc: Training ML models to filter environmental noise and calculate practical pest risk indices.
roadmap_stages.stage7_desc: Developing actionable watering advisory logic based on microclimate trends and crop growth stages.
roadmap_stages.stage8_desc: Building multilingual SMS, WhatsApp, and voice-assisted farmer alert channels.
roadmap_stages.stage9_desc: Multi-site pilot trials with progressive farmers, FPOs, and agronomy research partners.

metrics.metric_accuracy_desc: True positive rate of acoustic threat alerts verified against manual field scouting ground truth.
metrics.metric_fpr_desc: Minimizing false alarms triggered by ambient wind, rain, machinery, or harmless insects.
metrics.metric_fnr_desc: Ensuring significant pest infestations are not missed during critical early stages.
metrics.metric_water_desc: Measuring volume of water saved through microclimate-guided watering vs. standard flood schedules.
metrics.metric_pesticide_desc: Tracking reduction in total chemical volume applied and timing alignment with actual pest pressure.
metrics.metric_loss_desc: Comparing harvested quality and yield between monitored blocks and unmonitored control zones.
metrics.metric_roi_desc: Quantifying net economic benefit (input cost savings + preserved yield) against system cost.

faq_page.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq_page.subtitle: Plain-language answers for farmers and partners. Tap 'Listen' on any question to hear the answer aloud.
faq_page.q1: Is the AgriVigil sensor safe for my crops and livestock?
faq_page.a1: Yes, 100%. AgriVigil is a completely passive listening and climate-sensing system. It does not emit harmful radiation, chemicals, or loud noises, and has zero negative effect on crops, cattle, or earthworms.
faq_page.q2: Does the system require continuous internet or Wi-Fi in the field?
faq_page.a2: No. The field unit is engineered for rural connectivity. It stores data locally and uses low-bandwidth cellular telemetry or SMS to transmit alerts, even in areas with weak 2G/3G mobile reception.
faq_page.a3: Commercial pricing is not yet decided. We are currently offering units as part of pilot trials to evaluate operational costs and ensure a clear, positive return on investment for farmers before commercial release.
faq_page.q4: Will AgriVigil work for my specific crop?
faq_page.a4: We are currently testing on priority crops such as cotton, paddy, sugarcane, pulses, and select horticulture crops. During the pilot phase, we will let you know if your crop is currently supported.
faq_page.q5: How does the sensor hear tiny insects in the field?
faq_page.a5: Insects produce minute sounds when chewing stems, walking on leaves, or moving underground. AgriVigil uses sensitive acoustic transducers and frequency filters to detect these biological sound patterns.
faq_page.q6: Can the sensor tell the difference between pests and rain or tractor noise?
faq_page.a6: This is one of the main engineering challenges we are solving. Our software is designed to filter out wind, rain, and machinery rumble so only sustained insect activity triggers alerts.
faq_page.q7: How does it help me save irrigation water?
faq_page.a7: The unit tracks field temperature and relative humidity continuously. This helps estimate crop water stress so you irrigate only when necessary, avoiding over-watering or pumping during extreme heat.
faq_page.q8: I cannot read well. How will I receive notifications?
faq_page.a8: AgriVigil is designed for high voice accessibility. You can receive voice call summaries or WhatsApp audio notes in Hindi, Punjabi, or your regional language.
faq_page.q9: How do I participate in the trial?
faq_page.a9: Simply tap 'Join Pilot' on our website, fill in your village and crop details (or use voice input), or call/WhatsApp us directly. Our field team will review your application.
